title: Redwood Optimize v1.2 — Product overview, PRD summary, design specs, roadmap, pricing & release notes
author: Priya Kapoor
body:
Overview:

Redwood Optimize v1.2 is the Q2 2026 release of our cost and performance optimization toolkit. The release focuses on two customer-facing capabilities: (1) autoscaling policies for Redwood Dedicated GPU pools with workload-aware burst handling, and (2) a new cost-suggestion engine that recommends batching, quantization profile, and model variant changes per route based on historical telemetry. This doc summarizes the PRD, design decisions, roadmap alignment, pricing/packaging impact, release notes, rollout/rollback procedures, owners, and follow-ups.

Goals (product-level):
- Reduce median per-token serving cost for typical generation workloads by 18–30% for Dedicated customers using recommended optimizations.
- Provide safe, SLO-aware autoscaling that reduces manual capacity management and supports burst capacity with automated fallback to cost-tiered variants.
- Deliver clear UX in Console and API for applying recommendations and tracking predicted savings.

Who this serves:
- Platform/infra teams operating Redwood Dedicated and Private deployments.
- Product/feature teams looking to reduce inference egress costs and improve tail latency under load.
- Solutions/consulting teams running cost assessments for customers.

PRD summary (high level):
1) Autoscaling policies for Dedicated pools
   - Feature: Policy objects that define min/max capacity, scaling metric (qps, 99p latency, GPU utilization), cooldowns, and burst budget.
   - Acceptance criteria: Pools will scale within configured bounds for 90% of synthetic replay tests; scaling events are observable and auditable in Console.
   - Owner: eng-platform + eng-sre (primary), product (PM).

2) Cost-suggestion engine (recommendations service)
   - Feature: A service that analyzes route-level telemetry for 7–30 day windows and emits ranked recommendations: batching size suggestions, quantization profile suggestions, model variant downgrades/upgrades for cost/latency trade-offs.
   - Acceptance criteria: Recommendations must include estimated cost delta, estimated latency impact, confidence score, and sample prompts used. UI must let customers simulate savings before applying.
   - Owner: applied-ml-and-evals + eng-serving-runtime + product.

3) Console & API UX
   - Feature: New Console pages and API endpoints under /recommendations and /pools/{id}/autoscaling for applying and auditing changes.
   - Acceptance criteria: Customers can preview, apply, and revert recommendations; audit logs are generated for automated changes.
   - Owner: eng-developer-experience + eng-platform.

Design specs (concise):
- Autoscaling policy schema (example YAML):

```yaml
policy_name: cost-aware-autoscale
pool_id: pool-1234
min_replicas: 2
max_replicas: 20
scale_by: 'qps' # supported: qps, gpu_util, p99_latency
target: 250 # target qps per replica when scale_by=qps
cooldown_seconds: 120
burst_budget: 1000 # tokens per minute that can be served beyond target using burst pool
fallback_model_variant: rwd-7b-quantized-v2
metrics_window_seconds: 300
```

Notes on metrics and safety:
- All scaling decisions are evaluated against per-route SLOs. A policy cannot scale below a configured floor if scaling would violate a route SLO.
- Autoscaler uses exponential backoff on repeated failures; scaling operations are reversible within 5 minutes.

- Recommendation scoring:
  - Input features: historical token counts, per-token latency distribution, KV/cache hit rates, model variant used, sequence length histogram, presence of streaming responses.
  - Output: {recommendation_type, estimated_monthly_savings_usd, estimated_p99_latency_change_ms, confidence_percent}. (Values surfaced in UI as text; internal schema kept normalized.)

Console UX specifics:
- Recommendation card with: short summary, estimated savings, confidence, sample prompts, and actions: Preview (simulate), Apply (create job), Schedule, Ignore.
- Audit trail entry created for each Apply and Revert with actor, timestamp, and diff.

Roadmap & themes alignment:
- Theme Q2 2026: Production economics — make inference cheaper and more predictable for Dedicated customers.
- This release maps to roadmap initiatives: "Autoscaling & Dedicated stability" and "Cost transparency and tooling".
- Next milestones: v1.3 (Q3) will add per-customer policy templates and native Private deployment support for autoscaler.

Pricing & packaging notes:
- Core recommendation engine features are included in Redwood Dedicated and Private v1 plans.
- Premium features (scheduled bulk-apply, white-glove optimization via consulting) are part of the Optimize Add-on SKU.
- Pricing change for Dedicated: no change to base Dedicated reservation pricing. We introduce a metered Premium feature priced at $0.02 per simulated optimization job for API-driven bulk simulations (pre-launch credit for early customers).
- Billing considerations: when recommendations cause model variant switches that result in different per-token billing, billable units reflect the model actually used post-change. Console shows an estimated billing delta pre-apply.

Release notes — Redwood Optimize v1.2 (2026-03-15):
Features:
- Autoscaling policies for Dedicated GPU pools (GA): define min/max replicas, scale metrics, burst budgets, and SLO-aware safety checks.
- Recommendation engine (Beta): route-level batching, quantization, and model-variant suggestions surfaced in Console with simulation preview.
- Console pages: new Recommendations dashboard, Pool Autoscaling tab, and Audit Trail entries for applied optimizations.

Improvements:
- Improved telemetry ingestion for route-level token histograms (reduces recommendation noise).
- New SDK bindings for the recommendations API (Python & Go).

Bug fixes:
- Fixed race condition in Dedicated pool scale-down path that could cause transient 429s under rapid churn.
- Resolved an edge-case where quantized variants reported incorrect throughput for streaming calls.

Known issues & limitations:
- Recommendation engine currently excludes streaming routes from batching recommendations (work in v1.3).
- Private deployment autoscaler requires v1.2 agent; customers on v1.0/1.1 must schedule an upgrade.
- Simulated savings can differ from real-world results if customer workload deviates strongly from the analyzed window (documented in UI).

Rollout plan & runbook (high level):
1) Staged rollout schedule:
   - Week 1 (canary): Internal Redwood Dedicated pools + 3 opt-in pilot customers; monitor SLOs and scale events.
   - Week 2 (gradual): 20% of Dedicated customer pools (randomized stratified by workload type).
   - Week 3 (general): 100% of Dedicated pools and Console availability for all tenants.

2) Monitoring & SLOs to watch:
   - p99 latency per-route (alert if > baseline + 25%)
   - Error rate 5xx/4xx (alert if > baseline + 5%)
   - Scaling failure rate (failed scale operations / total) > 1%
   - Autoscale churn (scale events per pool per hour) > 6 -> investigate oscillation
3) Rollback criteria:
   - Any sustained p99 latency regression > 50% for production routes across canary customers for > 15m.
   - Scaling failure spike > 5% across canary pools for > 10m.
Rollback steps (numbered):
   1. Disable autoscaling for affected pools via Console (Pools > {id} > Autoscaling > Toggle Off).
   2. Revert any applied recommendation jobs using Audit Trail -> Revert action (applies reverse change).
   3. If issue persists, escalate to eng-platform oncall and open an incident: runbook reference confluence/eng-platform/runbooks/autoscale-incident-runbook.

Post-release follow-ups (tracked in product JIRA):
- v1.3: add streaming-aware recommendations, Private agent v1.2 rollout automation, per-customer policy templates.
- Metrics: add per-route cost baseline dashboard and a nightly re-evaluation job for recommendations to reduce staleness.
- UX: A/B test default presentation of recommendations to improve apply-rate while minimizing risk.

Appendix — example API calls (reference):
- GET recommendations for route:

curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" "https://api.redwood.com/v1/routes/{route_id}/recommendations?window_days=14"

- POST apply recommendation:

curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"recommendation_id":"rec-9876","apply_mode":"dry_run"}' "https://api.redwood.com/v1/recommendations/apply"
